memories.author: D04
memories.text:
- Irritable bowel syndrome
  - Status: Chronic abdominal bloating, alternating diarrhoea and constipation, symptoms present 3–4 days/week.
  - Plan: Start mebeverine 135 mg BD, ispaghula husk 5 g OD, loperamide 2 mg SOS for diarrhoea. Advise low‑FODMAP diet: breakfast – oatmeal with lactose‑free milk; lunch – rice with steamed carrots; dinner – grilled fish with zucchini. Review in 8 weeks.
- Weight: 62 kg
- Waist: 84 cm (female cut‑off 80 cm – slightly increased)
- Due: HbA1c – not applicable (no glucose‑lowering therapy)

mebeverine 135 mg – 1-0-1 – after food
ispaghula husk 5 g – 1-0-0 – with water before breakfast
loperamide 2 mg – 0-0-1 SOS – after food if loose stools

memories.author: lab
memories.text:
CBC: Hb 12.8 g/L (12‑16), WBC 6.2 ×10⁹/L (4‑10), Plt 210 ×10⁹/L (150‑400)
Stool routine: No ova, cysts, or occult blood
 tTG‑IgA: <4 U/mL (negative <7)

memories.author: patient
memories.text: Over the past week I’ve had more bloating after meals and two episodes of watery diarrhoea. The ispaghula husk seems to help a little but I still feel uncomfortable.

memories.author: front_desk
memories.text: Follow‑up appointment booked for 2025-07-10 at 10:30 am with Dr Karthik Hegde (D04).

memories.author: D04
memories.text:
- Irritable bowel syndrome
  - Status: Bloating reduced to 1‑2 days/week, diarrhoea episodes down to once weekly. Patient reports mild constipation on days without loperamide.
  - Plan: Continue mebeverine 135 mg BD. Reduce ispaghula husk to 3 g OD. Add loperamide 2 mg BD only if >3 loose stools/day. Diet: breakfast – poha with peanuts; lunch – khichdi with curd; dinner – chapati with bottle‑gourd sabzi. Review in 3 months.
- Weight: 61.5 kg
- Waist: 83 cm (still above 80 cm cut‑off)
- Due: HbA1c – not applicable (no glucose‑lowering therapy)

memories.author: lab
memories.text:
CBC: Hb 13.0 g/L (12‑16), WBC 5.8 ×10⁹/L (4‑10), Plt 205 ×10⁹/L (150‑400)
Stool routine: Normal flora, no parasites

memories.author: D04
memories.text: Abdominal ultrasound: Liver normal size, no focal lesion. Gallbladder wall thickness 2 mm (normal). No biliary dilation. Both kidneys normal. No significant bowel wall thickening visualized.

memories.author: D04
memories.text: Referral to Dr Suman Rao, Gastroenterology, Vikram Hospital, for opinion on refractory IBS symptoms and to rule out microscopic colitis. Include recent labs and ultrasound report.

memories.author: D04
memories.text: Gastroenterology opinion: Symptoms consistent with IBS‑M. Recommend low‑FODMAP diet trial for 6 weeks, consider rifaximin 550 mg BD for 14 days if bloating persists. No endoscopic abnormalities noted; colonoscopy not required at this time.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: Following the gastroenterologist’s advice I started a strict low‑FODMAP diet. Bloating has improved markedly; I have only occasional mild discomfort after lunch. No diarrhoea episodes in the last two weeks.

memories.author: D04
memories.text:
- Irritable bowel syndrome
  - Status: Patient reports good symptom control on low‑FODMAP diet, bloating 1 day/week, bowel movements regular. No need for loperamide in past month.
  - Plan: Continue mebeverine 135 mg BD. Continue ispaghula husk 3 g OD. Discontinue loperamide SOS (keep as rescue). Reinforce low‑FODMAP diet: breakfast – idli with coconut chutney; lunch – rice with lentil soup and carrots; dinner – roti with pumpkin sabzi. Review in 3 months.
- Weight: 61 kg
- Waist: 82 cm (approaching cut‑off)
- Due: HbA1c – not applicable (no glucose‑lowering therapy)

memories.author: D04
memories.text:
- Irritable bowel syndrome
  - Status: Stable on low‑FODMAP diet and mebeverine. Occasional mild bloating after heavy meals, no diarrhoea. Patient reports improved quality of life.
  - Plan: Continue mebeverine 135 mg BD. Continue ispaghula husk 3 g OD. Keep loperamide 2 mg SOS as needed. Reinforce diet: breakfast – upma with vegetables; lunch – millet pulao with raita; dinner – chapati with paneer‑palak. Review in 4 months.
- Weight: 60.5 kg
- Waist: 81 cm (just above female cut‑off)
- Due: HbA1c – not applicable (no glucose‑lowering therapy)
